explanation: The arrow operator (->) is commonly used to access members of a pointer to a class object.  Overloading this operator allows you to create custom behavior when accessing members through a pointer-like object, often used to simulate pointer semantics for classes that don't directly use pointers. This is particularly useful in smart pointer implementations and other situations where you want to provide a clean and intuitive interface while managing resources or other underlying complexities.
keywords: operator-> overloading, arrow operator overload, smart pointer operator->, member access overload
